Thullatun min al-awwalin (56:13–14): "A large company from the earlier generations, and a few from the later ones" — these will be a limited number, extremely pure people, and among the earlier ones they will be more numerous. Reports differ on who these people are. The first view is that they are the lofty figures who hastened toward faith, those who responded first to the call of some prophet from among the earlier nations before Islam, while the later ones are those who hastened to Islam first and endured trials in the path of Islam. The second view is that the earlier and later ones are from the Muhammadan community (ummah Muhammadiyyah): the earlier ones are the people of the first era (al-salaf al-salih), and the later ones are those who came in the subsequent periods. This view has been preferred by ʿAllamah Ibn Kathir, and reports have also been related from al-Hasan and Ibn Sirin in support of this preference. Abu Hatim narrated, through al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah, from ʿAffan, from ʿAbdullah ibn Bakr al-Sahmi, that he heard al-Hasan, when he recited the verse:

﴿Wa al-sabiqun al-sabiqun. Ulaika al-muqarrabun﴾ (56:10–11): "And the foremost, the foremost — those are the ones brought near," he said: "The foremost have indeed passed away from this world; O Allah, make us among the companions of the right (ashab al-yamin)." Then he narrated, from his father, from Abu al-Walid, from al-Sari ibn Yahya, that al-Hasan recited:

﴿Wa al-sabiqun ... al-awwalin﴾ (56:10–13) and he said: "Most of those who hastened have passed away from this world."

He also narrated to me, from his father, from ʿAbd al-ʿAziz, from Ibn al-Mughirah al-Minqari, from Abu Hilal, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, that he recited:

﴿Thullatun min al-awwalin wa qalilun min al-akhirin﴾ (56:13–14): "A large company from the earlier ones and a few from the later ones." He said they used to say (or hope) that all of them would be from this ummah.

Having given these details about who these people will be, the Qur'an now describes the blessings prepared for them in the Gardens, in a form that they can imagine, comprehend, and enjoy. Besides these blessings, there will be other blessings there, for whose perception and enjoyment they will then be ready, and these are blessings that no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and that have never occurred to the heart of any human being.

This is their hospitality on that Day, concerning which they were in doubt. They kept asking about it and were not ready to confirm the Qur'an. On the other hand, they also committed shirk and were not afraid of the warning of that Day.

Here the fate of all the groups comes to an end, and that great event, which will turn everything upside down, occurs; and with it the first phase of this Surah concludes.

As for the second phase, it takes the Islamic worldview as a whole, although the clearly evident aspect in it is the matter of resurrection and gathering. From this second phase it becomes clear with what beauty the Qur'an addresses human nature, how it presents proofs, and with what simplicity it penetrates into people's psyche, although the subject matter consists of the lofty topics of ideas and philosophy.

The miracle of the Qur'an is that it draws from the affairs of the heavens, which keep proceeding in their routine, such points as become the great issues of the universe. It derives the laws of nature from facts and scenes that lie before everyone's eyes. From them it forms a worldview, and it makes the events that bring spiritual growth, awakening of consciousness and sharpness of the senses the focus of thought and vision. It creates in human consciousness awareness about the phenomena that people see day and night and pass over heedlessly like the negligent, and it tells man that you are immersed in miracles that surround you day and night.

The Qur'an does not hand people over to a few limited miracles that were found within some limited time and place; rather it shows them the miracles within their own selves. It finds miracles among the ordinary events present in their environment. It does not take them away from the cosmic phenomena near them in order to entangle them in complex philosophy, or merely to discuss rational obligations, or to demand scientific experiments that not everyone can perform. Islam does not prescribe for people any such philosophical theology. The Qur'an's approach is different.

People's souls are created by Allah. The natural phenomena around people are also created by Allah. Whatever Allah has created in this world is a miracle. This is the Qur'an of Allah. Therefore it leads them to the miracles that are within their own selves and within their environment. It explains to them those miracles which they see day and night. They see them, but the miraculous aspect of these phenomena is hidden from their eyes, because through seeing this process day and night they have come to regard it as a routine matter. The Qur'an opens their eyes regarding these very events. It tells them what the secret of all this divine power is, how much unity is found within them, and how this divine power is working within your souls just as it works within this universe which is around them, within which are the proofs of faith and the evidences of truth. In this way Islam unfolds these things before human nature and awakens human nature.

The Qur'an adopts this very approach in this lesson. First of all, before them are presented those proofs of miraculousness which are in their own creation. Then those that are in their crops which they sow day and night; is the water they drink not of little miraculousness? This fire which they kindle: this fire burns in your hearths morning and evening. Then before your eyes the deaths of your relatives take place; these people set out on the journey of the Hereafter. This moment is destined to come upon every person, and every living being must stand before the Lord of irresistible power from which there is no escape. All stratagems and all excuses come to an end.

The manner in which the Qur'an addresses nature is itself, by its very style, among the proofs of its miraculousness: that the Qur'an is from the Creator. The source of the Qur'an is the same from which this universe has proceeded. Therefore the Qur'an derives great truths from the simple phenomena and forms of worldly life and places them before man in a natural voice. A particle, about which it is said that it is the first unit of the whole universe, and the cell, which is the first matter of life: the particle is itself a miracle and the living cell is itself a miracle. Here the Qur'an derives religious beliefs from a most simple manifestation, from phenomena that every human being experiences. Human lineage, agriculture, water, fire, death: every human being has practical dealings with these things. The cave dwellers too were acquainted with the life of the embryo, and they were acquainted with the growth of vegetation, with rain; they kindled fire and the hour of death came upon them. From the material of these observations the Qur'an forms a great theological belief, doctrine and philosophy, because the Qur'an is the book of every human being and these observations are those which every human being encounters. These are great cosmic truths, yet they are commonplace; they are lofty secrets, yet open before every person. In this whole discussion there is also a far-reaching hint, which is towards the positions of the stars, a subject of the study of nature, and an ordinary person and a great scientist both observe the setting-places of the stars.

By the setting-places of the stars is meant the engineering of the universe, and this is both a great secret and a commonplace matter. Then life and plants are both miracles. Then water is indeed the essence of life, and fire, and now electricity is the first sign of civilization.

To look at existing and observed things in this manner, to study them, and to derive from them thought, belief, doctrine and system has not been the method of human knowledge and teaching. Whenever humans have debated these issues, they have never placed these cosmic materials and phenomena before themselves; and when they have ever tried to see them, they have made them complicated and have not taken them with the simplicity with which the Qur'an took them. Rather, humans have made even these simple phenomena into a complex philosophical problem, turning them into a riddle, and the common people of the world have gained no benefit from it.

But Allah in His Book has adopted a natural approach, that is, for lofty issues He has also used material that is comprehensible to the common people, so that whatever conclusions were drawn from it became near to people's understanding; just as Allah has established the continuity of life within the creation of this universe with great ease, similarly from this universe He has proven the Lord of the worlds in a simple manner. Please observe.

Creation, death and the end: life and death are an event that every person experiences in their own self and also witnesses in the lives of others. Then what is the reason that they do not affirm that Allah has created them? This truth presses upon a human being to such a degree that for a person there is no recourse except to believe in God.

﴿Nahnu khalaqnakum fa-lau la tusaddiqun﴾ (56:57): "We created you, so why do you not affirm it?"

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 56, verses 58–59:

﴿Have you considered the semen that you emit? Is it you who create it, or are We the Creator?﴾ (56:58–59)

The human role in procreation, whether in creation or in reproduction, is simply this: a man deposits the semen in the womb of his wife. After that, the role of both of them ends. (Test-tube baby techniques have eliminated even this.) Now this weak fluid works under the supervision of the Lord, the Exalted. Only the hand of Divine power operates in its creation, its nurture and its growth. It gives it form, it gives it a soul, and from the very first moment through all the stages, there are nothing but miracles upon miracles. At every stage there occurs an extraordinary miracle in which no one besides Allah has any role. Mankind, to this day, has not even reached the reality of this very method of creation and reproduction. They do not even know how this miracle happens. The thought of their participation in it does not even arise?

This much reflection is available to every human being, and it is sufficient for understanding this miracle and being affected by it. But the story of this cell, from the moment it was placed in the mother's womb until it became a complete human being, is stranger than imagination. If this story did not continually take place in practice, and if this human being did not see it night and day, the human intellect would never have believed it.

This cell then begins to divide. It keeps growing, and within a short time, in place of that single cell, many millions of cells appear. Each of these cells possesses characteristics distinct from the others, because each one creates a particular aspect. Some are bone cells, some are muscle cells, some are skin cells. From these cells eyes are formed, from these cells the tongue is formed, and from these cells glands are formed. The cells of the glands have an even more specific nature. Every cell knows where it has to go and work. For example, eye cells do not wander by mistake into the stomach or into the feet; but if they are artificially taken to the back, they will form an eye there. Yet the cells that receive the command and inspiration from Allah gather in the place of the eye and form the eye right there. Likewise, ear cells do not go to the feet in order to form an ear there. All these cells, in accordance with the command and inspiration of Allah, shape this human being in the best form and according to the best design. Under their watch and in this formation, man has no role at all.

This is the beginning of man. As for the end of man, it is even stranger than this, although man, seeing it day after day, is not moved by it.

And you have certainly known the first creation, so why do you not take heed? (56:62) "You already know your first creation, so why do you not take a lesson?" And this second creation is very near, and there is nothing in it that should be a matter of wonder.

In this simple manner and with this easy approach, the Qur'an presents the matter of the first creation and the resurrection. Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 56, verses 63–67:

Afara'aitum ... mahrumun (76) (6 5:4 6 tak

﴿Have you ever considered: these seeds that you sow, do you cause them to grow, or are We the ones who cause them to grow? If We willed, We would reduce them to chaff, and you would be left astonished, saying, "We have been burdened with debt! Indeed, we have been deprived."﴾

These agricultural plants grow before their eyes and yield their harvest. The point to consider is what role they play in this. These people plough the land and place grain or seed in it, which Allah created. After that, their role ends, and the hand of power (dast-e-qudrat) takes over, and the plant completes its stages in a miraculous manner.

This seed or grain begins the process of reproducing its kind, and it travels its path in such a way that it seems to be an intelligent and watchful thing, moving straight along its way and passing through its stages. A human may make a mistake in his work, but this seed makes no mistake. It acts according to the method that Allah has ordained for it. It never misses its appointed target, because it is guided by the hand of power, and this is a wondrous journey. It is a journey that, if it were not repeated before our eyes day and night, reason would not confirm it, and the imagination could not conceive of it. Otherwise, what reason could believe that within this small grain of wheat there exist the stalk, the leaves and the grain, or that within a date pit there exists a tree so tall?

If these things were not repeated before us day and night, reason would not accept them, and no thought would turn toward them. But because this story is repeated before all people, and this journey is completed morning and evening, people accept it. And who is there who would claim that, apart from sowing the seed, he has any other role in this process?

People say, "We grew the crop, and we produced this much yield," although their role in all these matters is very limited. As for the whole process that the seed passes through, and the miracle that from the heart of a small seed a great tree comes into being, all of this is an attribute of the Creator. If Allah did not will it, no seed would display this miracle. This story would not reach its end in this way, and if Allah willed, He would reduce the seed to chaff before it could yield. This is the will of Allah.

If this were to happen, people would make painful remarks about it: "Innā lamughramūn" (indeed we have been burdened with debt), meaning, there has been a loss; "bal naḥnu maḥrūmūn" (rather, we are deprived and unfortunate). But it is Allah's grace that He gives them fruit, and these grains complete their cycle. Human life is also like this. The human cell also does the same. In this way, the power of Allah creates a human being. Is it difficult that Allah cannot bring forth human beings again from this same earth? ... What is it in the resurrection of the Hereafter that you find strange?

**Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 56, verse 76:**

"And indeed, it is a great oath, if you only knew" (56:76). But today, how much do we know of how great this oath is? Our knowledge is far greater than that of the first addressees, although even our present knowledge is very limited, and we cannot fully conceive the greatness of the positions of the stars.

The little knowledge that has been acquired about the positions of the stars has been acquired through our very small observatories, whose range of sight is very limited. The information obtained through these observatories is that the number of other clusters of stars is not known, and their boundaries have not been determined.

"Scientists say that stars and planets, whose number is more than several billion stars, cannot be seen with the naked eye alone. They can be seen only through telescopes and observatories, and without seeing them, these machines and instruments also cannot perceive them. All of them are floating in this dark and unknown celestial space, and there is no possibility that one star will come within the magnetic sphere of another star, or collide with another star, just as there is no possibility that a boat sailing in the Mediterranean Sea will collide with a boat sailing in the Dead Sea, when both are moving in the same direction and at the same speed. Just as this possibility is remote, so too the collision of two stars is impossible." (Allah aur Science, p. 33)

Each star has been placed at such a distance from its neighbouring star, and placed with such wisdom and planning, and the attraction of all these stars has been balanced in such a way that it is in balance with the billions of stars that move and float in this boundless space. This is one aspect of the greatness of the position of the stars. But although our conception of greatness is far greater than that of the addressees of the Qur'an at that time, the conception of future generations will consider even this broad conception of ours to be limited.

"And indeed, it is a great oath, if you only knew" (56:76). This allusion to the oath, and then not swearing it, is a style: it is a more effective and heart-touching manner, and the matter settles more firmly in the mind, because there is no need for an oath upon it.

فی کتب مکنون (6 5: 87) "In a Book well-guarded." Its explanation is given by the following verse.

لا یمسہ الا المطھرون (6 5: 97) "Which none touches except the purified." The polytheists alleged that the Qur'an had been brought down by the devils (shayatin). This is a refutation of their allegation, because a devil cannot touch the Book that is in Allah's knowledge and under His protection. It is brought down by pure angels.

This is the best explanation of this verse, because the particle لا (lā) is نافیہ (nafiyah, negating), meaning that the act is simply impossible. It is not ناہیہ (nahiyah, prohibiting), meaning "do not do this," because in this world both the pure and the impure touch the Qur'an, and believers and disbelievers also touch it. Therefore, in this sense, the negation is not realised at all. Rather, the meaning that is closer, and that is correct in reply to the disbelievers' allegation, is that the purified (al-mutahhirun) refers to the angels, because heavenly scriptures are beyond the reach of the devils.

And the verse that follows it:

تنزیل ............ العلمین (6 5: 08) "It is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds." It is not brought down by the devils. This supports the meaning above.

If the narrated traditions (ahadith) give another meaning, that no one should touch the Qur'an except a pure person, then Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)... [the text here refers to such narrations]. However, Allamah Ibn Kathir said: "This is a valuable point. al-Zuhri recited it in this manner, but this interpretation should not be adopted. This hadith has been narrated by al-Daraqutni as a musnad (a report traced directly back to the Prophet) from Amr ibn Hazm, Abdullah ibn Umar and Uthman ibn Abi al-As, but there is room for criticism in all of its chains of transmission."

After this comes the last paragraph of this surah. It is the final plectrum on the strings of reason and understanding. In it, there is mention of the moment that, when a person thinks about it, his limbs tremble. This is the moment of death, about which there is no doubt, after which a person does not return, and from which no one can escape.

Translation:

The phrase ﴿وَأَنتُمْ حِينَئِذٍ تَنظُرُونَ﴾ ("while you are looking on") ............ (6 5:4 8) shows that around him stand relatives, helpless and at a loss.

Now the soul has departed from this world, and the deceased has left everything behind in the world. He is stepping into a new and different world. Now he has only what he has earned. He has no control over the good and evil that remain behind. In that new world he sees all of this, but he cannot turn back and tell anyone anything. He has become separated from his surroundings. A body lies there, which the onlookers see, yet they do not know what is passing over it. Here the limits of human power and human knowledge come to an end. At this point human beings acknowledge that they are helpless and powerless. They have a very limited capacity. Now there is no dispute left ..... Here the curtain falls on this scene; nothing is seen, nothing is known, and no movement is visible on the scene.

Now there is only the power of God. Only the knowledge of God remains. All affairs are in the hand of God, and in this matter there is no longer any doubt, not even a trace of doubt; there is neither argument nor stratagem.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 56, verse 85:

"...and We are nearer to him than you, but you do not see." (56:85)

Here the scene turns to the majesty of Allah (Shan-e-Bari). The fear of Allah overspreads the atmosphere. Allah is ever present and watching at all times, but the Qur'an has this remarkable quality that it awakens the dormant consciousness of man. Thus, in the gathering at death, the atmosphere becomes even more awe-inspiring through the conscious presence of Allah, while all the people are frightened, terrified and helpless, and there is an atmosphere of farewell, farewell.

In such an atmosphere a challenge comes forth. In this most trembling, regretful and lamenting gathering, and in this extremely grievous atmosphere, a challenge comes from Allah.

﴿Then why, if you are not to be judged, do you not bring it back, if you are truthful?﴾ (56:86–87)

"Now, if you are not under anyone's authority and you consider yourselves truthful, then at that moment why do you not bring back the soul that is departing?" If the matter is as you say, that there is no reward and punishment and you are free, then when the soul has reached the throat, send it back from there, for it is going to give account and it is departing while you are present. You stand there helpless, and it is going to answer for a great responsibility, while you remain silent and powerless, standing by.

Now all discussions come to an end. Every argument is refuted.
